Article Title: ‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
Article Text:
“So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,” Hasina said (Photo: Reuters).

Hasina alleges crackdown on Awami League members

Hasina raises concern over influence of extremist groups

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday reiterated her commitment to return to Dhaka in December despite a death sentence awaiting her return from India.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email.“So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,” Hasina said.The former leader has served as Prime Minister of Bangladesh for one term from 1996 to 2001 and four consecutive terms from 2009 to 2024.In 2024, Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government. In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal ordered her death sentence for crimes against humanity. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to the United Nations data, cited by AP, nearly 1,400 were killed during the unrest.The former PM has denied wrongdoing, rejected the tribunal's verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her. However, New Delhi said the request was being legally examined.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” India’s high commissioner to Dhaka Dinesh Trivedi remarked during an October discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.On Wednesday, Hasina told the AP that she was aware of the risks she could face on returning, but had no intention of changing her decision.“I know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,” she told the news agency.Hasina did not specify how she intended to travel back to Bangladesh from India.Her proposed return comes as her Awami League party faces an uncertain political future. The party remains banned, while several of its senior leaders have been arrested or forced into exile.Hasina alleged that at least 20,000 party members had been killed since August 2024. She also claimed that thousands had been arrested, tortured or driven into hiding, while supporters had lost their homes, businesses and livelihoods because of their political affiliations.“There is no normal political or democratic environment,” she said, accusing the authorities of systematically targeting the party.Following Hasina's removal from office, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus headed an interim administration for 18 months. In February, Tarique Rahman, son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and a longstanding political rival of Hasina, won a landslide victory in an election held under the interim government. The Awami League was barred from contesting the polls.Several rights organisations, including Human Rights Watch, have criticised Rahman's government over alleged violations of civil and political rights in recent months. The government has maintained that arrests have been made in connection with specific charges.Hasina also expressed concern over the growing influence of hard-line groups in Bangladesh, saying the political climate had allowed extremist elements to gain confidence.“The present political environment has allowed extremist elements to become more confident,” she said.Global rights groups and independent observers had earlier raised concerns about radical groups seeking to suppress liberal forces during the Yunus-led interim administration. Minority communities have also reported facing intimidation.The interim government denied the allegations. The current administration has continued to face criticism over the deteriorating law and order situation in the country.Hasina, who took a tough stance against radical groups during her 15 years in power, said she was worried about their growing influence.Asked whether she expected countries such as the United States and India to press Bangladesh to ensure her safe return, Hasina said she was not seeking protection from foreign governments.“I value friendship and cooperation with all nations. That has always been our (Bangladesh's) foreign policy. But I do not need the blessing of a foreign power to return to my own country,” she said.
Article Summary: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Dhaka in December. Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before the Delhi Police Crime Branch on Thursday in connection with the October 13 Jantar Mantar protest, which led to their detention on charges of trespassing at the denotified protest site.The two CJP leaders reached the Crime Branch office in Rajouri Garden after being summoned to join the investigation. Fellow leader Ajinkya Shinde was also summoned in the case.Das, Ranka and Shinde had earlier skipped questioning scheduled for October 22. Ranka had said they could not appear on the scheduled date and had informed the police about their inability to attend. The leaders were awaiting fresh dates for questioning, he had said."We are waiting to hear from them. We have not received a specific date yet. We could not make it on the previous date, and we had informed them about that. They said they would confirm the timings, so we are waiting for the Crime Branch to get back to us," Ranka had said.The police had detained Das and Ranka following the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. According to the police, the leaders entered the area through private premises and violated conditions imposed to maintain peace.The two CJP leaders were released from judicial custody on October 21 by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court after furnishing personal and surety bonds and submitting written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.In their undertakings, Das and Ranka promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before the Delhi Police Crime Branch on Thursday. They were detained on charges of trespassing at the denotified protest site. Fellow leader Ajinkya Shinde was also summoned in the case.

Article Title: 'Respect seniors, end BJP-RSS hatred': Rijiju's seven-point advice to Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , listing seven conditions that he said the opposition party should follow if it wants to "win more MPs".In a post on X, Rijiju said Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" and stop promoting their agenda. He also urged the Congress leader to respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, saying it was part of Indian tradition.Listing the conditions, Rijiju asked Gandhi to "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently."He further advised him to "end deep hatred against BJP, RSS and Modi Ji" and "treat BJP as political opponent, not enemy."The minister also asked Gandhi to take "Parliament more seriously" and allow MPs to participate in debates and discussions."Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he said, listing the final two conditions.Rijiju's remarks came amid an ongoing exchange between the ruling BJP and the Congress over Rahul Gandhi's demand for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Earlier on Wednesday, Rijiju shared a video clip of his speech in Parliament during which opposition leaders had walked out of the House."Parliament is the House for debates & discussion. But people who don't believe in democracy, debates and discussion are talking about debate," the parliamentary affairs minister said.Meanwhile, Rahul renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate, claiming that he could establish within five minutes that the prime minister was a traitor. His remarks drew a sharp response from Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.Following Rahul's challenge, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged the prime minister to come forward and answer questions raised over alleged vote theft.In a post on X, Kharge said Modi had no answers on the "vote chori" issue and should accept Gandhi's challenge to debate various subjects, including "foreign connections"."You don't come to Parliament. You have not done a SINGLE OPEN PRESS CONFERENCE; it's time you came for a DEBATE.“Come forward, Face Questions. Tell the Nation why did you indulge in VOTE CHORI !!” Kharge said.“PM Modi is parroting his flop line of ‘Dimaagi Naxal’! He has NO answer on Vote Chori and the Open Challenge by Rahul Gandhi to discuss how he mortgaged Indian interests to Foreign powers!” he added.Kharge also questioned Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks about three crore voters being "ghuspaithiyas" (infiltrators), asking what he had been doing as home minister if illegal immigrants had entered the country.“He should be sacked for his incompetence,” the Congress president said.Responding to Rahul's challenge, Sitharaman said Parliament was already an appropriate venue for a debate and reminded him that he was the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha."Rahul ji, you ask the Prime Minister to choose a venue for a debate. There is already one: Parliament, where you happen to be the LoP."Just yesterday, Home Minister Shri Amit Shah offered a special session to debate SIR and EVMs. Why not show the same enthusiasm for a debate in Parliament that you show while issuing challenges on social media?" Sitharaman said on X.She said that demanding answers also required Rahul to stay and hear the government's response."Demanding answers also carries an obligation to hear them," she said, alleging that Gandhi and other Congress leaders had walked out of Parliament on several occasions while the government was responding to their allegations.Sitharaman also accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies of repeatedly disrupting parliamentary proceedings, resulting in entire sittings being washed out.She further questioned the nature of Gandhi's allegations and asked him to present specific claims backed by evidence."Simply throwing together a long list of accusations doesn’t make your case any stronger. As LoP, you are expected to show some seriousness and responsibility."You say, 'Daro mat'. Then bring the facts, face the scrutiny and stay to hear the answers. In the House, uphold the standards of debate you demand from others," she said.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju lays down 7 conditions for Rahul, takes swipe at Congress leader. Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" Gandhi should respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, he said. Gandhi renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate.

Article Title: Srinagar MP’s exit part of BJP’s ‘Op Lotus’ plan in J&K, says NC

SRINAGAR: Governing National Conference (NC) in Jammu & Kashmir Wednesday described the resignation of its Srinagar MP, Aga Ruhullah Mehdi, as the handiwork of BJP , saying the party had succeeded in its mission under ‘ Operation Lotus ’.Addressing a news conference at the party headquarters in Srinagar, NC legislators Salam Sagar and Sajad Shaheen said the MP’s departure was the outcome of a “planned and calculated” strategy.“BJP has succeeded in getting Aga Sahib (Mehdi) out of NC. He has now joined a force that has tried two or three times over the past 80-90 years to weaken us, but we managed to defeat those attempts earlier,” Sagar said.“What you witnessed yesterday (Tuesday) in Kashmir is similar to ‘Operation Lotus’ carried out in Parliament to engineer defections and get MPs to leave their parties. With Aga Sahib’s help, BJP’s agenda has been fulfilled,” the NC MLAs alleged.The duo termed Mehdi’s allegation that NC had abandoned its fight for restoration of J&K’s special status an excuse and ruse. “He (Mehdi) was with the party for 24 years. If he failed to realise in all these years that we are not sincere in following our agenda, as he has alleged, then it speaks about him, rather than the party,” Sagar said, adding: “We will never compromise on Articles 370 and 35A or the rights of the people of Jammu & Kashmir.J&K deputy chief minister Surinder Choudhary accused BJP of misleading the NC MP, referring to its national vice-president Ram Madhav’s reported remark in Jammu on Tuesday that Mehdi held a rally in Budgam after his resignation with the blessings of “our people”.“Aga Sahib was a good and respectable person. BJP misled him, and Ram Madhav himself said yesterday said that Aga Sahib was their man,” Choudhary told media persons in Jammu on Wednesday.Responding to the allegations, BJP spokesperson Sajjad Yousuf Shah said the party had nothing to do with NC’s internal affairs. ‘Operation Lotus’ was a figment of NC’s imagination, he said, insisting that Ram Madhav was in Jammu under a preplanned party programme and his visit had nothing to do with the crisis in the governing party.
Article Summary: NC legislators Salam Sagar and Sajad Shaheen said the MP’s departure was the outcome of a “planned and calculated” strategy. ‘Operation Lotus’ carried out in Parliament to engineer defections and get MPs to leave their parties.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav on Wednesday accused the BJP and RSS of targeting his father, Lalu Prasad Yadav , through central agencies and attempting to weaken the Constitution and democracy. He also criticised Dhirendra Shastri over his alleged remarks about Lord Krishna.Addressing a gathering of the Yadav community at the Sadar Festival, organised by the Telangana government at Hyderabad's NTR Stadium, Tejashwi said his community drew strength from its association with Lord Krishna."Look at how much Modi ji and the BJP have harassed Lalu ji. They unleashed all the country's agencies - the ED, the CBI, and the Income Tax Department - upon him, and even sent him to jail. Even at his age, he is still forced to make appearances in court. Yet, Lalu ji continues to fight - even at this age - because we are descendants of Krishna," he said."We are Yadavs; we fear no one, and Lalu ji has never bowed down. Even if Modi ji tries to use the threat of prison to intimidate us, we will not be afraid. After all, our Lord Shri Krishna himself was born in a prison..." he added.Accusing the BJP of trying to undermine democratic institutions, Tejashwi said the RJD would continue to defend the Constitution and democracy.“You may do whatever you please - you seek to destroy the Constitution and crush democracy - but we will work to protect our nation's democracy and its Constitution. We will ensure that the RSS is reduced to dust; we will teach you a lesson!” he said.The RJD leader also took aim at religious preacher Dhirendra Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Baba whom he referred to as 'Thageshwar Shastri'. He accused the preacher of making inappropriate remarks about Lord Krishna ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.“Friends, a certain 'Shastri' has appeared - just in time for the UP elections - a 'Thageshwar Shastri'. The RSS and the BJP are busy dividing human beings, and now, at Modi ji's behest, this 'Thageshwar Shastri' has begun dividing the gods themselves. He has made highly inappropriate remarks about our Lord Krishna. If such people come to Hyderabad or Telangana, the Yadav community should give them a 'warm' welcome - and we shall do the same in Bihar!. ..” he said.The remarks came amid a controversy over purported videos of Dhirendra Shastri circulating on social media. The videos triggered criticism over alleged derogatory comments about Lord Krishna and comparisons involving Lord Ram.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also criticised the alleged remarks, questioning the intentions behind them and calling for action against those responsible for disturbing social harmony.In a post on X, Akhilesh said, “Who are these anti-Sanatana elements acting on the behest of? First, a controversial video about Lord Krishna surfaced, and now disrespectful remarks about Lord Rama's father are being spread. Its political masters may tolerate all this, but we will not accept even a fraction of it.""All its programs should be cancelled for the crime of disrupting social harmony. Now, true Sanatanis will write their account," he added.

Around 10 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel were feared missing after two boats allegedly capsized during an operation to rescue stranded fishermen in Bethupalli lake in Telangana's Khammam district on Wednesday evening.According to news agency PTI, the personnel were conducting a rescue operation in two boats in the swollen lake, located in Sathupalli mandal, when the boats were suspected to have capsized. They had been deployed to rescue a group of fishermen stranded in the lake.Khammam district, which borders Andhra Pradesh, has been receiving heavy rainfall under the impact of cyclone Murasu.Khammam district collector Divakara T S and other officials rushed to the site and deployed teams to search for the missing personnel.Telangana revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said in a post on X that rescue teams had identified the possible location of the missing SDRF personnel.He said the personnel would be rescued safely.Chief minister A Revanth Reddy, who was briefed about the incident, directed the District Collector to make every effort to rescue the missing personnel, according to an official release.He also asked Chief secretary Sanjay Jaju to monitor the situation.Union minister of state for home Bandi Sanjay Kumar said National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) personnel had been deployed and were carrying out rescue operations.“Deeply concerned over SDRF personnel going missing during an operation to rescue fishermen stranded in floodwaters at Bethupalli Lake in Sathupalli, Khammam district, Telangana,” Kumar said on X.He said he had spoken to the Khammam district collector to assess the situation and coordinated with senior NDRF officials to deploy rescue teams.“We are closely monitoring the situation and remain in constant coordination with the authorities to ensure the safe return of everyone involved,” Kumar said.Search and rescue operations were continuing, with teams working to locate the missing personnel.
Article Summary: Around 10 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel feared missing. Two boats allegedly capsized during an operation to rescue stranded fishermen in Bethupalli lake in Telangana's Khammam district. Search and rescue operations are continuing to locate the missing personnel.

Article Title: Prez can be prosecuted after leaving office but not ECs, says petitioner
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, with a pending plea raising a similar issue. The provision bars courts from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against serving or former CECs and election commissioners for acts done or purported to be done in discharge of official duties.A bench told lawyers for Manoj Jha and Arun Agrawal that the cases would be tagged with the pending matter.Jha's plea argues that Section 16 gives officials wider protection than President, MPs, and SC and HC judges, covering civil and criminal proceedings during tenure and for life, without exceptions for corruption, mala fides or crime. It says President may be prosecuted after leaving office, while a former election commissioner arguably cannot."A member of Parliament who takes a bribe to vote can be tried but an EC who takes a bribe while "purporting" to act in office arguably cannot. A sitting judge of this court can be prosecuted with sanction yet a retired election commissioner cannot be prosecuted with or without it. The Constitution places no functionary above the law, however Section 16 of the CEC does," the plea said.Agrawal's plea said the wording "is or was" creates lifelong immunity, while "purporting to act" could cover conduct outside lawful authority. It said the provision contained no good-faith condition and could bar prosecution for corruption, forgery and other serious offences.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. A bench told lawyers for Manoj Jha and Arun Agrawal that the cases would be tagged with the pending matter.

Article Title: Two scrap collectors die in Srinagar fire, CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 4L relief
Article Text: SRINAGAR: Two scrap collectors, including a minor, were killed in a fire that engulfed around 80 makeshift shelters in Durbal, Bemina, on the outskirts of Srinagar early Wednesday, officials said.The blaze erupted around 12.30am. Police identified the deceased as Mohammad Noor Alam (27) and Al Ameen (16), both from Delhi. The flames also damaged an empty poultry farm and a tipper.J&K CM Omar Abdullah condoled the deaths and announced ex-gratia relief of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased. He also directed authorities to ensure immediate relief and all necessary assistance to the affected families.

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday responded to Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a public debate, saying the discussion should take place in Parliament rather than on the streets.In a post on X, Sarma took a swipe at the Rae Bareli MP over his Diwali greeting to the Prime Minister, in which the Congress leader had wished Modi on the festival while holding a rose.“Dear Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day, not on Diwali. Anyway, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will see you in Parliament,” Sarma wrote.In a video shared on X, the Assam chief minister questioned whether Rahul was aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition and said Parliament was the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.“Rahul ji, yesterday you posted a video. You were holding a rose and wishing the Prime Minister a Happy Diwali. Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day; they are not given on Diwali. Tell me one thing: are you even aware that you are the Leader of the Opposition? If you are the Leader of the Opposition and if you truly consider yourself to be one, then where is this debate with the Prime Minister supposed to take place? On the streets? In some alleyway? Or in Parliament?” Sarma said.He also referred to the presence of the Lok Sabha Speaker and members of Rahul's family in Parliament, arguing that the debate could be held there.Sarma said several issues, including the Bofors controversy and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, could be taken up during a parliamentary debate. He urged former Congress president to initiate the discussion and ensure that proceedings were not disrupted.“There are plenty of issues to discuss, from Bofors to the Bhopal Gas Tragedy. This time, please ensure there is no ruckus in Parliament. You should initiate the debate; the Prime Minister will respond, and all these issues can be addressed,” he said.Questioning the Congress leader's call for a public face-off outside Parliament, Sarma added, “Why do you want to drag people out onto the streets? This isn't Bangladesh; this isn't Nepal. Rahul ji, do not take the people for fools.”He further advised the Congress leader to move away from what he described as the role of an “angry young man” and participate in a peaceful debate in Parliament.The Congress MP had issued the challenge in a post on X on Tuesday, urging PM Modi to agree to a public debate in the presence of the media and the country's youth.“It’s been 24 hours since I challenged you, Modi ji. You say the opposition is anti-national. Choose any stage, any venue, and debate me on this - Who is anti-national? Who has connections with foreign forces? And what is the nature of those connections? Let’s do this as soon as possible. Daro mat!” Rahul wrote.Proposing a format for the discussion, the Congress leader said both leaders could sit across a table, with the Prime Minister free to appoint the moderator.“We’ll both be there. The media will be there. The youth of this country will be there. There will be a table. You’ll sit on one side, I’ll sit on the other. You can appoint whoever you want as the judge. You can even make Mohan Bhagwat ji the judge,” he said.Rahul also listed several issues he wanted to raise, including the financial system, the India-US deal, the Adani case and the Epstein matter.“There will be questions about the financial system, the financial structure, how the US deal happened, why it happened and why so quickly, why you made the deal alone and didn’t inform the Cabinet, why the Adani case was closed, Epstein - and many other issues. We’ll discuss all of them openly.Let the truth come out. Let everything be crystal clear,” he added.The Congress leader also challenged PM Modi to file a defamation case against him over his allegations, saying he was already facing several such cases.“You make allegations against me, don’t you? Come forward. Everything will become clear. You’ve filed defamation cases against me over other matters. I think there are around 45 defamation cases against me. But on this issue of the debate, on the question of foreign connections, you haven’t filed a defamation case. Go ahead, file one. We’ll discuss that openly too. Happy Diwali, Modi ji,” Rahul wrote.
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma responds to Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi for a public debate. Sarma questions whether Rahul is aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition. He says Parliament is the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.

Article Title: Indian tourist killed, PIO injured as copters collide during Everest rescue
Article Text:
Indian killed as copters collide during Everest rescue

Here's what happened

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With agency inputs)

A 47-year-old tourist from Chennai was killed and two others - an Indian-origin New Zealand citizen and a pilot - were injured when two helicopters collided barely about 10 feet above a helipad near Mt Everest on Tuesday. The accident occurred around 8.11am at Pheriche, 12km south of Everest Base Camp, as one helicopter was evacuating tourists stranded by heavy snowfall and the other was carrying cargo.The rotor blades of the two choppers struck each other as both aircraft attempted to land, sending them crashing onto the snow-covered helipad. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower in Lukla - gateway to the Everest region. The accident is believed to be Nepal's first mid-air collision involving two helicopters.The deceased was identified as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, who died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen, and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Balaramudu and Patel were being evacuated aboard a private Fishtail Air Airbus AS350 helicopter, registration 9N-AJR, which had taken off from Gorakshep, a remote settlement near Everest Base Camp at an altitude of approximately 5,164 metres.The other helicopter, an Air Dynasty AS350 registered 9N-AOD, had flown from Lukla carrying cargo. Its pilot, the sole occupant, escaped unhurt. Verified footage showed the helicopters approaching the helipad from different directions, with one descending faster than the other.The weather appeared clear, with no visible signs of strong winds. People nearby rushed towards the wreckage immediately after the collision. “Preliminary reports suggest miscommunication between the pilots, as the area is outside the coverage of Lukla Airport’s air traffic control tower and pilots have to communicate with each other,” said Mukesh Dangol, director general of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal.“We are recording the statement of the injured pilot,” he added. CAAN spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said, “It appears the accident happened when two helicopters attempted to land at the same spot.” The aviation authority has launched an investigation to establish how both aircraft came to approach the helipad simultaneously. Solukhumbu district official Kaman Singh Thapa Magar also confirmed that the weather was clear at the time but raised the possibility of a technical problem.Prajapati and Patel were flown by a Prabhu Air helicopter to Nepal Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu Valley.Air Dynasty confirmed that its pilot was uninjured, contradicting initial reports that both pilots had sustained injuries. Balaramudu’s body was first taken to Lukla and later transported to Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu for a post-mortem before repatriation to India.India’s foreign ministry said the Indian embassy in Kathmandu was coordinating with Nepalese authorities to bring back Balaramudu’s remains. Pheriche, at around 4,300 metres, is a key stop along the Everest trekking route. Heavy snowfall had disrupted trails and left tourists stranded at high-altitude settlements, including Gorakshep, prompting helicopter evacuations. Expeditions are under way on Everest and nearby Ama Dablam.With no road access to the upper Everest region, choppers are widely used to ferry climbers and supplies, besides carrying out rescues.
Article Summary: Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, 47, died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.

Article Title: 'Shawarma law' not 'Sharia law': Abdul El-Sayed's remark goes viral after senate win - watch
Article Text:
'Shawarma law' remark goes viral as Abdul El-Sayed makes history with Michigan Senate win

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think will be the most significant outcome of the recent midterm elections? Increased representation for diverse groups A shift in national policy Greater voter engagement 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The US midterm elections have delivered a major victory for Democrats, with the party making significant gains across the country and flipping control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.Among the notable victories was that of Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, whose remarks about implementing "shawarma law" instead of "Sharia law" have gone viral on social media.El-Sayed, 42, an epidemiologist and former public health official aligned with the Democratic Party's progressive wing, defeated Republican candidate and former representative Mike Rogers in one of the country's closely watched Senate races, NBC News projected. His victory makes him the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.In his victory speech, El-Sayed introduced himself by his full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, before using Arabic expressions to take a swipe at Republicans and Vice-President JD Vance.“My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed,” he said, before explaining his repeated use of the Arabic expression "inshallah", meaning "God willing", during the campaign.“Up until right about now, you might have noticed I always say “inshallah”, or “God willing”, whenever the outcome of this race was mentioned. But today, tonight, we can turn that inshallah into alhamdulillah. For the rightwing ops, that just means “praise be to God,” OK?”He continued his remarks with a reference to Vance, saying, “JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January.”El-Sayed also used his speech to criticise US support for Israel and speak about the situation in Gaza, condemning the abuse faced by those who have raised concerns about the conflict.“See, they try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers without being murdered by our tax dollars,” he said.“Michiganders, we want our taxes spent here, for schools here, and healthcare here, and infrastructure here. We don’t want our money sent to do apartheid or genocide or war.”El-Sayed's victory came despite a campaign marked by Islamophobic attacks from President Donald Trump and other Republicans. Trump had called him a “communist” and described him as a “jihadist” and a member of the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood.He also faced a setback in the final days of the campaign when Democratic Representative Haley Stevens, whom he had defeated in the party's primary, withdrew her support and endorsed Rogers after attending church with the Republican candidate.El-Sayed had defeated Stevens to secure the Democratic nomination earlier this year, challenging the party establishment with a campaign centred on progressive policies. He advocated for universal healthcare through the Medicare for All proposal and called for an end to US military aid to Israel.Republicans had portrayed the general election as a referendum on the Democratic Party's progressive wing, making the contest between El-Sayed and Rogers one of the most closely watched Senate races in the country.His win also extends the Republican Party's long-running electoral drought in Michigan. Republicans have not won a Senate seat in the state since 1994. El-Sayed will succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters.His victory was among several electoral breakthroughs for women, candidates of colour and other underrepresented groups in Tuesday's elections. Democrats made significant gains in key statewide races and flipped control of both chambers of Congress, riding a wave of dissatisfaction with the Trump administration.The results also pointed to gains for Democrats in traditionally conservative states, with analysts, civil rights leaders and grassroots voter organisations suggesting that the party had attracted Republican voters while rebuilding support among its traditional constituencies.Black and Latino voters, in particular, had emerged as increasingly contested groups in recent election cycles, as the latest results reshaped the political landscape and expanded representation in the highest levels of American government.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed, 42, is the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. He defeated Republican candidate Mike Rogers in one of the country's closely watched Senate races. In his victory speech, he used Arabic expressions to take a swipe at Republicans and Vice-President JD Vance.

Article Title: Bomb scare forces Aer Lingus Dublin-Rome flight to make emergency landing at France airbase

Article Title: 45-year-old woman changing bedsheet plunges 15 feet into hidden Scindia-era chamber as floor caves in at historic house in Madhya Pradesh’s Bhind
Article Text:
45-year-old woman fell into an underground pit due to a floor collapse at her home.





BHOPAL: A 45-year-old woman fell nearly 15 feet into an underground pit, taking her bed down with her, when the floor of a room collapsed at a historic house in Bhind on Wednesday night.The house, once a Scindia-era administrative court, sits atop an old chamber that was used to store grain collected as tax. She was changing the bedsheet when the ground gave way, said sources.The incident occurred at approximately 9:15 pm at a residence in Girls School Wali Gali. Family members and neighbours rescued her by lowering a ladder into the pit. She was admitted to hospital with injuries, and her condition is reported to be stable.According to the family, the premises functioned as a local administrative court during the Scindia State period and was used for revenue collection and administrative work in the surrounding areas. Grain collected as tax was stored in an underground structure locally known as a “galla khanti.” The cavity that opened on Wednesday is believed to be part of this original structure.The family said their great-grandfather, Pandit Madan Mohan Mishra, served as an honorary magistrate under the Scindia State and was also entrusted with duties related to the Van Khandeshwar Mahadev temple, say locals.The house was reconstructed in the 80s, and the family says the pit was sealed at that time. They suspect that years of water seepage gradually washed away the soil inside the abandoned structure, leaving a hollow beneath the floor that eventually gave way under pressure. Water was found at the bottom of the pit.Most household members were attending an invitation when the accident occurred and returned to find the woman trapped inside. The exact cause of the collapse and the condition of the underground structure have yet to be established.
Article Summary: A 45-year-old woman fell nearly 15 feet into an underground pit, taking her bed down with her. The floor of a room collapsed at a historic house in Bhind on Wednesday night. The house sits atop an old chamber that was used to store grain collected as tax.

Article Title: Telangana bus conductor dies 10 days after woman passenger pushes her off moving bus
Article Text:
Gundla Pravalika succumbed to her injuries ten days after she was pushed off a bus (R: File photo used for representation)

Woman picked fight over 10, say police

HYDERABAD: Ten days after she was allegedly pushed off a moving bus by a woman passenger, Gundla Pravalika, a conductor with the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC), succumbed to her injuries at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday.She had sustained grievous injuries in the incident at Mittagudem Centre in Aswapuram mandal of Bhadradri-Kothagudem district.Following Pravalika’s death, Aswapuram police altered the case against the accused, B Mounika, from attempt to murder to murder.“The accused, who was arrested earlier, continues to be in judicial remand,” Ch Yallaiah, station house officer of Aswapuram police station, told TOI. “Although the conductor received treatment, she died due to blood loss. The victim was unmarried,” he added.The incident occurred on October 25, when Pravalika was on duty, operating a bus between Manuguru and Bhadrachalam along with driver K Jampaiah.A heated argument reportedly broke out between Pravalika and Mounika over change for the bus fare. During the altercation, Mounika allegedly pushed the conductor out of the moving bus, causing her right leg to come under the rear wheels.The 24-year-old conductor was rushed to a local hospital, where she received initial treatment. She was subsequently shifted to a private hospital in Hyderabad for further treatment, but succumbed to her injuries.Chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed grief over Pravalika’s death and conveyed his condolences to her family. “He conveyed deep condolences and sympathy to her family members.The CM stated that the state govt will stand by Pravalika’s family and provide help,” the Chief Minister’s Office said in a post on X.Following the CM’s instructions, the state govt announced a job for Pravalika’s mother, a house for the family under the Indiramma Housing Scheme and an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh. The family will also be provided insurance cover of Rs 1 crore, transport minister Ponnam Prabhakar said.The minister visited Osmania General Hospital, where Pravalika’s postmortem examination was conducted.According to police, Mounika boarded the bus around 9am on the day of the incident at the Manuguru flower market, accompanied by her son. She availed herself of a zero-fare ticket by furnishing her Aadhaar card and handed Pravalika a Rs 100 note to purchase a half ticket, priced at Rs 10, for her minor son.“When the female conductor asked for Rs 10 in change, the accused refused. This led to an argument, and the accused allegedly hurled abuses at the victim,” a police officer said.The bus was subsequently stopped, and Mounika was asked to get down. However, she refused and insisted that the RTC staff drop her at the point where she had boarded the bus, police said.As the driver resumed the journey, the argument reportedly continued. When the bus reached Mittagudem Centre, Mounika allegedly pushed Pravalika out of the moving vehicle, causing her serious injuries.Mounika had claimed that the conductor was standing on the footboard and had accidentally fallen off the bus. However, other passengers reportedly contradicted her account, alleging that Mounika had pushed Pravalika.
Article Summary: Gundla Pravalika, a conductor with the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC), succumbed to her injuries at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday. She had sustained grievous injuries in the incident at Mittagudem Centre in Aswapuram mandal. The case against the accused, B Mounika, has been altered from attempt to murder to murder.

Article Title: Watch: Hot oil spills on 3 as woman rams SUV into kebab centre in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Sajina Begum accidentally drove her SUV into Halevuru kebab centre, injuring three men (Visuals credit: X)





BENGALURU: Police have issued a notice to a woman who, on October 28, rammed her SUV into an eatery near Bannerghatta, injuring three men.According to an FIR registered with Bannerghatta police, the Mitsubishi Pajero Sport was driven by Sajina Begum, wife of Safrulla Abdul Aziz, a businessman hailing from Keralam and resident of Electronics City Phase I.In her statement, Begum told cops that she felt giddy when the vehicle came near ‘Halevuru kebab centre’ on CK Palya Road and, in a state of confusion, pressed the accelerator instead of brakes.Gaining sudden speed, the SUV entered into the kebab centre and rammed into the materials, including a vessel containing hot oil.The oil spilled on worker Basavaraj and customers Munikrishna and Manjesh, causing minor burn injuries. Also, a couple of motorbikes placed outside the kebab centre were damaged. After two days of treatment, the injured men were discharged from the hospital, police said.The complaint was filed by Paramesh A, whose bike was damaged in the mishap.“Soon after the accident, the woman had promised to pay the expenses towards the repair of my motorbike. Also, she promised to look after the medical expenses of the injured; but so far, nothing happened and therefore, I am filing the complaint,” Paramesh said.A senior police officer said Sajina Begum and Safrulla Abdul Aziz were regularly purchasing kebab from the same shop.“That day too, they had come to buy kebab, but the accident took place. Aziz claimed he had paid around Rs 75,000 towards the medical expenses of the injured ones. Matter will be clear once Sajina appears before us and gives a statement,” he said.
Article Summary: Sajina Begum accidentally drove her SUV into Halevuru kebab centre, injuring three men. Begum told cops that she felt giddy when the vehicle came near the eatery. The oil spilled on worker Basavaraj and customers Munikrishna and Manjesh.

Article Title: DU professor Sangit Ragi’s office ransacked after row over ‘casteist’ slurs
Article Text:
Sangit Kumar Ragi's office at Delhi University faced a violent protest following his controversial remarks during a television debate





NEW DELHI: The office of Sangit Kumar Ragi, a Delhi University professor, was allegedly ransacked by a group of people Wednesday, a day after his remarks against Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka in a television debate triggered a row over casteist slurs.Videos that have surfaced show a group of people entering the social sciences building on North Campus, where Ragi’s office is. They shouted “haye-haye” and demanded Ragi’s suspension.Some of them allegedly smeared cow dung on the gate of his office, covering the nameplate. They allegedly broke the glass pane on the office door, tore and scattered files and damaged furniture. The videos also showed people smearing cow dung inside the office.DU officials who did not wish to be quoted said the university was yet to file a police complaint. The protesters have filed a police complaint against Ragi.Ragi said he would not file a a police complaint as they were students. He said he believed they were from Samajwadi Party’s student outfit.Speaking to TOI, he said the protesters were angry about his remarks during the TV debate, which he admitted he should not have made.“It was a reaction to a fellow panelist. I am not a politician, and I feel I should have restrained myself and perhaps ignored his comments about me. I have personally apologised to him and also issued an apology online,” he said.The All India Students’ Association (AISA) held a separate protest outside Ragi’s office Wednesday and burnt his effigy. The organisation demanded his resignation over the alleged casteist remarks.In the November 3 TV debate, Ragi and Kaka started arguing during a discussion on remarks by Bageshwar Dham’s Dhirendra Shastri. Videos of the exchange circulated on social media. Ragi was heard using a casteist slur against Kaka, who too had used derogatory language against Ragi.Following the backlash, Ragi issued an apology on X Tuesday evening. He said Kaka had repeatedly made personal attacks against him. His response was aimed at people who use abusive language and not at any community, Ragi said.This, however, is not the first time Ragi has faced criticism over remarks during a television debate.In August, his comments about Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had led to complaints before the university’s vice-chancellor and at Parliament Street police station.
Article Summary: Sangit Kumar Ragi's office at Delhi University was allegedly ransacked by a group of people. His remarks against Samajwadi Party spokesperson Manoj Kaka in a television debate triggered a row over casteist slurs. The protesters have filed a police complaint against Ragi.

Article Title: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi made a phone call to Sharad Pawar to inquire about his health condition





PUNE: PM Narendra Modi Wednesday requested NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar , 85, who was discharged from a private hospital, to focus on his health, saying his daughter and Baramati MP Supriya Sule would take care of the country along with him.“PM Modi called up Pawar saheb this morning to enquire about his health. He spoke with great warmth and respect and suggested that Pawar saheb should take complete rest,” Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Sharad Pawar, told the media.Maniyar said Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on his recovery.“PM told Pawar saheb that Supriya is ready and that he, along with Supriya, will look after the country, while Pawar saheb should focus on his health,” Maniyar said.Pawar thanked the PM for enquiring about his health and assured him that he would take rest. Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune on Monday morning after complaining of pleuritic pain.After undergoing treatment for two days, he was discharged on Wednesday.In a statement, Dr Purvez K Grant, managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, said, “He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling from the hospital to his Mumbai residence.”
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi made a phone call to Sharad Pawar to inquire about his health condition. Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune on Monday morning after complaining of pleuritic pain. After undergoing treatment for two days, he was discharged on Wednesday.
