GUWAHATI: Three militants were killed and at least four others injured in a gunfight between rival Naga groups in Manipur ’s Noney district Wednesday morning. Hours later, suspected militants opened fire on passenger and goods vehicles along the Imphal-Ukhrul road in Ukhrul district but there were no casualties.The gunfight occurred between Zeliangrong United Front-Jenchui (ZUF-J) and a combined team of Zeliangrong United Front-Kamson (ZUF-K) and National Socialist Council of Nagalim (NSCN-IM) at Taodaijang village.Two of the dead belonged to ZUF-J, a cessation of operations (CoO) agreement signatory with the Centre, and one to ZUF-K.The clash follows a statement from ZUF-K on Nov 1, accusing ZUF-J of collaborating with security forces. ZUF-J signed a cessation of operation with the Centre in 2022.NSCN-IM, headquartered at Hebron in Nagaland, is a long-standing pan-Naga armed and political group that seeks a unified homeland, “Nagalim”, covering Naga-inhabited areas of Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and parts of Myanmar. It has a significant presence in Manipur, the home state of its supremo, Th Muivah.ZUF was formed in 2011 to represent the Zeliangrong people, who are also a major Naga community comprising the Zeme, Liangmai and Rongmei, as a regional outfit and operates primarily in localised pockets, mainly in Tamenglong and Noney districts in Manipur.In the second incident, at about 4.45 pm, suspected militants opened fire on passenger vehicles and a goods-laden truck near TM Kasom village in Ukhrul district. The vehicles were headed to Ukhrul from Imphal and had been escorted by security forces up to Litan, after which the personnel withdrew.According to reports, the firing using sophisticated arms reportedly lasted nearly 10 minutes. Passengers took cover, and all occupants escaped without physical injuries.In Kangpokpi district, the Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU), Sadar Hills, extended its total shutdown by 48 hours, until 5 pm on Nov 6. It accused govt of failing to act decisively over the killing of two Kuki-Zo civilians and to implement its charter of demands.The violence comes a day after chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh directed security agencies to identify active armed groups, excluding those engaged in peace talks with the state govt, suspected of involvement in the recent violence. He asked agencies, including the Army and central paramilitary forces, to report on the groups’ involvement at the earliest and warned that govt would consider declaring such groups unlawful if their involvement in violence against civilians is established.Manipur govt also ordered setting up peace committees in all districts, chaired by district magistrates, to restore peace and normalcy. The move followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s query to chief minister on communal harmony efforts. It is the second such initiative after a 2023 committee set up by the MHA failed to deliver results.The committees will include the SP, sub-divisional officers, department officials, community leaders, civil society groups, journalists, doctors, teachers and retired officials. They will facilitate inter-community dialogue, identify tensions and rumours, counter misinformation, recommend confidence-building measures and help restore safe movement and essential services.They will meet at least fortnightly, record proceedings and report to the home department. They will be consultative bodies and cannot exercise the powers of the district administration or police.
Article Summary: Two of the dead belonged to ZUF-J, a cessation of operations (CoO) agreement signatory with the Centre, and one to Zuf-K. Hours later, suspected militants opened fire on passenger and goods vehicles along the Imphal-Ukhrul road in Ukhrul district.

Article Title: Beheaded, body dumped in graveyard: How a seven-month salary dispute ended in grisly murder
Article Text:
In an attempt to conceal the victim’s identity, the accused allegedly returned to the spot early on Nov 3 and severed the head from the body.

Dispute over Rs 30,000 in alleged salary deductions

Police crack case, recover severed head





SURAT: Beheaded and dumped in two different locations, a textile worker's body was found in a cemetery in Surat, while his severed head was recovered near railway tracks beneath the Alkapuri bridge in Katargam.Police have arrested his 54-year-old co-worker, who allegedly killed him over a seven-month salary dispute.The accused, identified as Sachitra Bal, a textile worker from Odisha, allegedly murdered Sanjay Khosla, with whom he worked at the same textile unit.According to police, Khosla maintained records of the working hours of all employees at the textile unit. Since Khosla earned more than Bal, the latter suspected that he was deducting money from his wages and pocketing it.Bal believed Khosla’s records had cost him Rs 160 daily for seven months, amounting to a loss of around Rs 30,000. The alleged deductions led to repeated quarrels between the two and strained their relationship.On November 1, Bal allegedly took Khosla to his residence in Rail Rahat Colony, Katargam, on some pretext.During the afternoon, he attacked the victim's neck with a sharp-edged weapon, killing him.After the murder, Bal allegedly stuffed the body into a sack and, late at night, dumped it in CNI cemetery near his residence after breaking a section of its boundary wall.In an attempt to conceal the victim’s identity, the accused allegedly returned to the spot early on November 3 and severed the head from the body. He then dumped it near the railway tracks beneath the Alkapuri bridge, around 3km away.After discovering the beheaded body, Katargam police launched an investigation and traced the murder to Bal. He reportedly confessed to the crime and disclosed where he had disposed of the head.Police subsequently recovered the head from near the railway tracks.Katargam police registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the BNS and Arms Act. Further investigation is underway to establish the exact circumstances of the financial dispute and the sequence of events leading to the murder.
Article Summary: Sachitra Bal, a textile worker from Odisha, allegedly murdered Sanjay Khosla, with whom he worked at the same textile unit. Bal believed KhosLA’s records had cost him Rs 160 daily for seven months, amounting to a loss of around Rs 30,000. The alleged deductions led to repeated quarrels between the two and strained their relationship. On November 1, Bal 'attacked the victim's neck with a sharp- edged weapon'

Article Title: BSF officer's 28-year-old son dies after falling from 10th floor of Gurgaon society
Article Text:
According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the BSF. (Image-Social Media)





GURGAON: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building at The Leaf Society in Sector 85 on Wednesday morning. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation.According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force (BSF). His father resides at Asia House on KG Marg in Delhi and is currently posted in Koraput, Odisha. The victim lived with his mother in a 10th-floor apartment in one of the towers at The Leaf Society. He was unmarried.Police said Ashim was generally quiet and had no known disputes with anyone. However, he was suspected to have been under mental distress for the past few days and rarely stepped out of his room.The family told police that Ashim was on the balcony on Wednesday morning when he fell. Hearing the noise, family members and other society residents rushed to the spot and took him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police from Kherki Daula police station reached the spot after receiving information and inspected the scene, including the balcony and the apartment.Police are investigating whether Ashim died by suicide or fell accidentally. Statements are being recorded from family members and other residents, while CCTV footage from the society is also being examined to establish the sequence of events.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation. According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force.

Article Title: Panchkula school assault case: 8-year-old granted bail; parents barred from giving him mobile phone
Article Text:
The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case (File photo)





PANCHKULA: The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB), Panchkula, has granted bail to the eight-year-old boy facing proceedings in the school assault case after his parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.The Class III student was represented before the board through his father.In the bail application, the parents undertook to take full responsibility for his care and supervision, while ensuring a healthy family environment, proper upbringing, education and moral guidance.They also assured the board that the child would undergo counselling, behavioural intervention and rehabilitation measures as advised by the competent authority.In addition, they undertook to provide him with appropriate medical care and all necessary support for his physical and mental well-being.The application stated that the child had cooperated with investigators and had no previous criminal record.It further argued that prolonged stay in custody could adversely affect his education, academic progress and overall development.The parents also assured the Board that they would ensure his presence whenever required and comply with all conditions imposed while granting bail.In a separate plea filed under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the boy’s father sought directions for the removal of videos, photographs and other content related to the case from social media platforms and public forums.The plea contended that such material could lead to the identification of the child and expose him to humiliation, discrimination and bullying.It also sought directions to the investigating officer and school authorities to prevent the further circulation of any material that could reveal the child’s identity.Acting on the application, the board directed authorities to ensure the removal of the assault video from social media within 15 days. The child had earlier been lodged in an observation home in Ambala.The board also directed that his studies should not be disrupted and ordered treatment after receiving a report from GMCH-32, which had recommended medical intervention after observing behavioural abnormalities.The matter is being pursued against the boy under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing simple hurt), 117(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) and 127(2) (wrongful confinement) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The case was recorded through a Daily Diary Report (DDR) at Sector 20 police station.
Article Summary: The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case. His parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.

Article Title: Bengaluru man beats daughter’s boyfriend to death after catching them together at home
Article Text:
The accused, identified as Anand





BENGALURU: A 22-year-old man from Kerala was allegedly beaten to death in Bengaluru after his girlfriend’s father caught him with his 19-year-old daughter at their house.The accused, identified as Anand, has been arrested.The deceased, Kiran, was a native of Thiruvegappura in Kerala’s Palakkad district.He was reportedly in a relationship with Anand’s daughter and also worked for him.Anand allegedly found the two together at his house and, in a fit of rage, assaulted Kiran. The injuries sustained in the attack led to his death.Anand, who is originally from Tamil Nadu and a native of Yelahanka, runs a company that manufactures machines used for preparing sweet corn. Police have taken him into custody and are investigating the case.
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Anand, has been arrested. The deceased, Kiran, was a native of Thiruvegappura in Kerala’s Palakkad district. Police have taken him into custody and are investigating the case.

Article Title: Amid protest by wife, Bihar government transfers IPS officer Bhanu Pratap Singh
Article Text:
Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification (Photo credit: X)





PATNA: The Home department on Wednesday transferred Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh and called him to police headquarters following days of protest by his wife, Pooja Singh, near the CM’s residence and outside the SP’s official residence, demanding that her family be reunited.The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one in an administrative reshuffle announced on Wednesday evening.According to the transfer order, Shailendra Singh, who was serving as SP in Sheohar, has been transferred to Khagaria as the new SP.Mohibullah Ansari has been shifted from Muzaffarpur City SP to Sheohar SP, while IPS officer Kumari Mamta has been given the additional charge of BMP-16.Pooja had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. On Nov 3, she moved her protest to outside the Khagaria SP’s official residence, reiterating her demand to reunite with her husband and daughter.According to Pooja, she married Bhanu in 2016 in a love marriage, when he was living in Delhi and preparing for the UPSC examination without a job.Puja alleged that she worked as a teacher at a private school to support the household expenses and financially helped her husband during his preparation.She said Bhanu subsequently cleared the UPSC examination and became an IPS officer of the 2021-batch.Pooja alleged that her husband’s behaviour changed after he joined the IPS and that their relationship had been strained for several months.She further claimed that she had not been allowed to meet their six-year-old daughter for the past eight to nine months. “I do not want to separate from my husband, nor do I want to initiate any legal dispute. I only want my family to be together again,” she had said.Pooja said she had repeatedly approached officials seeking intervention in the matter but had not been able to resolve the dispute. Her central demand, she maintained, was to reunite with her husband and daughter and rebuild their family life.Home department’s transfer order came against the backdrop of her protests. However, the order does not specify whether the transfers are directly linked to the domestic dispute.
Article Summary: Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification. Pooja Singh had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one.

Article Title: Smoking, bike rally, songs: Man accused of murdering 16-year-old boy gets hero's welcome after bail
Article Text:
Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail.





SATNA: A man accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy in Madhya Pradesh's Satna district allegedly staged a show of strength on the streets shortly after being released on bail after spending around 14 months in jail.The accused, identified as Man Singh alias Betu Singraul, was welcomed with garlands outside the jail before his supporters took out a bike rally. A video showing him sitting on the bonnet of a Bolero SUV and smoking a cigarette during the procession has gone viral on social media.The rally was reportedly taken out from the jail to Siddharth Colony, with several supporters joining the procession on motorcycles and in vehicles. The incident has raised questions over law and order and whether traffic rules were flouted during the procession.Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown under the jurisdiction of Kolgawan police station, during which a gunshot was allegedly fired. Satyam was shot in the chest during the altercation. He was rushed to hospital but died while being taken to Rewa for treatment.Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail. However, his grand welcome outside the prison and the subsequent procession have triggered controversy.The viral video has also raised questions about the alleged violation of traffic rules and the possibility of public intimidation during the procession. It remains to be seen whether Satna police will take action over the incident.While bail is a legal right, the incident has brought the conduct of the accused and his supporters on public roads under scrutiny.
Article Summary: Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown. Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail.

Article Title: 2 killed in Chawri Bazaar building collapse: MCD suspends assistant engineer, junior engineer over negligence; FIR ordered against contractor
Article Text:
3-storey building collapses in Delhi's Chawri Bazaar

What happened at Gali Sitara?

No building plan sanctioned: MCD





NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has suspended an assistant engineer and a junior engineer following the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar, which killed two people and injured four others on Thursday.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has also ordered an inquiry into the incident and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor.The action against the MCD officials was taken after the Deputy Commissioner of the Old Delhi Zone found a prima facie case of serious negligence in the discharge of their duties.The suspended officials have been identified as Assistant Engineer (Building) Mohd Naeem and Junior Engineer (Building) Aman Dalal.In separate office orders, the Deputy Commissioner placed both officials under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry.“In view of the recent incident and the developments arising therefrom, and considering the prima facie case of severe dereliction of duty, you are hereby placed under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry,” the orders stated.The three-storey building under construction collapsed in Gali Sitara, near Chawri Bazaar Metro station, around 9.50am on Thursday.More people were initially feared trapped under the debris, officials said.Two people were killed after being trapped under the rubble. A Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team pulled out two bodies from the debris, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by local residents before the fire department teams arrived.The identities of the deceased are yet to be established, police said. Multiple teams, including personnel from the Delhi Fire Services, were deployed to carry out rescue operations.A senior MCD official said the plot on which the three-storey building collapsed measured 50 square metres.No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, and the civic body had not received any complaints regarding its construction.The official said the building was still under construction, although work had been stopped around 15 days before the collapse.According to officials, workers were removing the support system beneath the roof when the building collapsed.The construction material used was non-engineered and had not set properly, which may have contributed to the collapse, they said.(Wiith agency inputs)
Article Summary: Three-storey building under construction collapses in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar. Two people killed after being trapped under the rubble. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has ordered an inquiry into the incident. No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, civic body says.

Article Title: Pentagon CTO Emil Michael: We helped Ukrainians a ton fighting Russia, but they invented the technology they actually needed because we didn’t have it and it is ...
Article Text:
Pentagon CTO: We were caught flat-footed

Stockpile growth, but Ukraine far ahead

Pentagon studying future battlefields

Cautious on AI targeting

Reiterates criticism of Anthropic

US still ahead of China in AI

The Pentagon’s technology chief Emil Michael has said the United States was unprepared for the rise of modern drone warfare and admitted that Ukraine had to develop some of the battlefield technologies it needed because the US could not provide them. Speaking at the WSJ Tech Conference, Michael said the conflict between Ukraine and Russia exposed significant gaps in America's military preparedness and accelerated efforts to expand the country's drone capabilities.Addressing the conference in Napa, California, Michael said the Pentagon had not anticipated how central drones would become to modern warfare. "We were caught flat-footed by the drone warfare in Ukraine and Russia," he said, adding that the US was not prepared because it "just didn't imagine it." He said the Defence Department is now focused on preparing for future conflicts and anticipating how warfare could evolve.Michael acknowledged that while the United States provided substantial support to Ukraine during its war with Russia, Ukrainian forces often had to create their own solutions on the battlefield. "We helped the Ukrainians a ton, but they invented what they actually needed because we didn't have it," he said.Michael said the US built about 1,000 drones under the previous administration, while its stockpile is now around 500,000. That is still a small fraction of the eight million to 10 million drones Ukraine estimates it will build this year, as its war with Russia nears a fifth year. Michael said the US helped Ukraine a great deal, but Ukrainian forces invented the technology they needed because the US did not have it.Michael said the Defence Department's Project Meridian has been tasked with examining what future warfare could look like, including potential conflicts underground and in space. The initiative includes participation from industry figures such as Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, and Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril IndustriesEven as the Pentagon pushes into cheap, autonomous systems, Michael said the military remains conservative about using artificial intelligence in combat. Developing targets still depends more on intelligence reports, satellite imagery and other human-led investigation than on AI, he said, adding that the US is not very sophisticated at AI-generated targeting.Michael declined to comment on the US strike in Iran last February that hit a girls’ school the US had mistaken for a military target. More than 100 people were killed, including dozens of children. The US has not released the findings of its investigation, and planning for the strike involved an AI targeting system. Michael said there must be appropriate human judgment at every level.Michael also reiterated his criticism of AI company Anthropic, which the Defence Department earlier designated as a national security threat. He said it was not difficult for the Pentagon to stop using Anthropic's models and noted that the department continues to use AI models from Google, OpenAI and Grok on its networks.On the global AI race, Michael argued that the United States maintains an advantage over China thanks to its access to advanced semiconductors and greater data-centre capacity.According to Michael, Beijing remains approximately six months to a year behind the United States in AI development, although he indicated that competition between the two countries remains intense.
Article Summary: Pentagon CTO: We were caught flat-footed by the drone warfare in Ukraine and Russia. He admitted that Ukraine had to develop some of the battlefield technologies it needed because the US could not provide them. Michael said the Pentagon had not anticipated how central drones would become to modern warfare.

Article Title: Ankita Bhandari murder case: Parents staging dharna at Rajghat removed by police
Article Text:
Bhandari's parents visited Rajghat on Wednesday to offer prayers and interact with the media.

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: The parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered at a resort in Uttarakhand in 2022, were removed from Rajghat after staging a dharna near the public gate of Mahatma Gandhi's memorial, sources said.The incident comes a fortnight after Bhandari's parents were detained by police while protesting against the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor near India Gate on October 14.Bhandari's parents visited Rajghat on Wednesday to offer prayers and interact with the media. They later staged a dharna along with two others near the public gate, which is not a designated protest site, a police source said.The group was repeatedly asked to disperse. However, after they refused to leave, they were removed from the spot. The source said they were not detained.During the incident, Bhandari's mother, Soni Devi, complained of health issues and was taken to Burari government hospital for a medico-legal examination (MLC). However, both she and her husband declined to undergo a medical examination, the source said.AAP MLA from Burari Sanjeev Jha and his supporters reached the hospital, following which Bhandari's parents left with the legislator.Bhandari, who worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Rishikesh, was killed on September 18, 2022. Her body was recovered from the Chilla canal four days later.Resort owner Pulkit Arya, son of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, and his two accomplices were sentenced to life imprisonment in the case.The case attracted political attention over allegations of the involvement of an unidentified VIP. Bhandari's family and activists have called for an investigation into this angle.
Article Summary: Bhandari's parents visited Rajghat on Wednesday to offer prayers and interact with the media. They later staged a dharna along with two others near the public gate, which is not a designated protest site, a police source said. The group was repeatedly asked to disperse. However, after they refused to leave, they were removed from the spot.

Article Title: 4 dead after Innova plunges into river near Gangnani on Gangotri National Highway
Article Text:
Innova car went out of control and plunged into a river





DEHRADUN: Four people were killed after an Innova car lost control and plunged into a river near Dabrani, around 20 metres beyond Gangnani on the Gangotri National Highway in Uttarakhand.The bodies of four people have been recovered from the riverbank, while a search operation is underway to check whether anyone else was travelling in the vehicle, officials said.The deceased have been identified as Smt Patel Ashokben (49), Ms Rutika Ashokbhai Patel (19), Shri Ghanshyambhai Sarvaliya (32), and the vehicle's driver, Surendra Singh, a resident of Haridwar.Meanwhile, 17-year-old Patel Vedant Ashokbhai sustained injuries and has been sent for medical treatment.Following reports of the accident, relief and rescue teams were mobilised on the instructions of District Magistrate Prashant Arya. Police, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel and teams from the 108 emergency service were rushed to the spot.The search operation involves the water police and divers, who are working amid strong river currents to locate any other possible passengers.The administration is monitoring the situation, with officials at the site directed to provide immediate assistance and expedite rescue efforts. The Disaster Management Centre and medical teams have also been placed on high alert to ensure that any survivors receive first aid and are shifted to hospital without delay.The cause of the accident is being investigated. Officials are also trying to establish contact with the families of those killed.
Article Summary: Bodies of four people have been recovered from the riverbank. Search operation underway to check whether anyone else was travelling in the vehicle. The deceased have been identified as Smt Patel Ashokben (49), Ms Rutika Ashokbhai Patel (19), and the vehicle's driver, Surendra Singh, a resident of Haridwar.

Article Title: Class 3 student dies after collapsing in Delhi school; family questions delay in medical aid
Article Text:
Class-III student dies after collapsing in classroom





NEW DELHI: A Class-III student of Lovely Heritage School in Mayur Vihar Phase-II died Wednesday morning after collapsing in her classroom.The exact cause of her death is yet to be ascertain-ed, though the principal claimed that doctors suspected a cardiac arrest.The family of Unnati Bharti (9) claimed that she didn't have prior medical issues and was fit when she was dropped off at school.Her relatives alleged that school authorities delayed medical assistance by taking her to a hospital in Nirman Vihar during peak-hour traffic, instead of nearby medical facilities. She was declared dead at the hospital.The principal, Bhawna Malik, countered the allegation, saying that a hospital near the school referred the girl to a better-equipped facility and the teachers accompanying her did the best they could at that moment.According to the school authorities, Unnati collapsed at 9:08 am at the fag end of the games period. "She was among several children who were returning to their classroom. After entering the class, she suddenly stood still and fell on her face and stopped moving," a school employee said on condition of anonymity.CCTV footage shows the girl trudging into the classroom with a hand on her waist. Seconds later, she stops, places both hands on her waist, and begins to sway before collapsing.The teacher immediately picked her up and seated her on a chair. However, she did not regain consciousness. The teacher then called for help, the school authorities said. Unnati's parents were informed about the incident at 9.18 am and police at 9.52 am.Her father, Vikas Bharti (38), who works as a contractual driver at Maulana Azad Hospital, claimed she was not taken to a better and closer medical facility like Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital or Max Hospital.Countering the allegation, principal Bhawna Malik said, "We immediately rushed her to Bimla Devi Hospital, the nearest medical facility. They asked us to take her to a better-equipped hospital. The teachers then took her to Malik Radix Healthcare in Nirman Vihar, which they thought was the best alternative. And it's not that far off."A police officer said the medico-legal case, which was received from Malik Radix, mentioned that Bimla Devi Hospital had indeed referred the child to a higher institute.Bharti said, "Unnati was physically active. Every mo-rning, she and I would exer-cise. Neither did she com-plain of any ailment, nor had she ever been diagnosed with any illness."Bharti said he dropped her off at school at 7:55 am. "My wife received a call at 9.18 am that our daughter had fallen down and hurt herself," he said, adding that the girl dreamt of joining the Navy when she grew up and was inspired by her grandfather, who had served in the forces.DCP (east) Rajeev Kumar said, "The footage shows the girl collapsing. Statements of her parents and the school authorities have been recorded. Investigators are examining the footage and other relevant evidence to establish the circumstances leading to her death. We are awaiting the postmortem report. No allegation has been officially raised as of now. Therefore, no case has been registered."
Article Summary: Unnati Bharti (9) collapsed at 9:08 am at the fag end of the games period. Her relatives alleged that school authorities delayed medical assistance by taking her to a hospital in Nirman Vihar during peak-hour traffic. The principal countered the allegation, saying that a hospital near the school referred the girl to a better-equipped facility.

Article Title: Delhi police file FIR on fake Russian minister video shared by Prashant Bhushan
Article Text:
Delhi Police has filed an FIR regarding a doctored video reportedly shared by lawyer Prashant Bhushan





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR over the alleged sharing of a doctored video of Russia’s foreign minister purportedly portraying an anti-India stance. The video was allegedly shared by Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan According to police, the matter came to light on Nov 3, during cyber patrolling. A social media handle reportedly flagged the alleged circulation of the video from Bhushan’s account.“Through the said video, there is an allegation of disseminating misleading, defamatory and inflammatory content to incite public disturbance and spread rumours,” Delhi Police wrote on X.Bhushan later told TOI, “I shared the video thinking it was genuine. It now appears that it was doctored. Before posting it, I had asked Grok (X’s AI chatbot) whether the video was real and it did not raise any red flag. Once I found out it was doctored, I deleted my post. Nothing offensive was said in the video.”The case was registered under sections 336 (4) (forgery), 353 (1) (statements conducing to public mischief), 356 (defamation), 340 (forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine) of BNS and 66C of the IT Act at a special cell police station.The video purportedly showed Russia’s minister saying that India was merely a trading partner and had no right to dictate or interfere in its foreign policy.The police action came after the ministry of external affairs (MEA) fact-checked the digitally manipulated video. “Fake Alert! The video of the Russian Foreign Minister being used in this post is fake!” MEA wrote on X.An X user also shared the altered video, prompting the Russian embassy in India to flag it as fake. “Please stop copying silly AI fakes,” the embassy posted on X.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has filed an FIR regarding a doctored video reportedly shared by lawyer Prashant Bhushan. The video purportedly showed Russia’s minister saying that India was merely a trading partner and had no right to dictate or interfere in its foreign policy. The police action came after the ministry of external affairs (MEA) fact-checked the digitally manipulated video.

Article Title: US midterm fallout: Trump's India envoy Sergio Gor may replace Marco Rubio - report
Article Text:
File photo: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor stand for the national anthem, as they attend a Freedom 250 reception at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

As Washington prepares to recover from the less than ideal performance of the Republican party during the midterms, reports suggest a possible overhaul in senior leadership.US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has emerged as a possible contender for senior positions in president Donald Trump's administration following the recent setbacks in the midterm elections, with his name reportedly circulating for roles including White House chief of staff and secretary of state.Gor, a former senior White House aide and close Trump ally, has been discussed within the administration as a potential candidate for a bigger role during the second half of Trump's term, according to a report by The Washington Sun, citing 10 people familiar with internal discussions. There is also growing speculation among State Department officials that Gor is interested in a promotion.Well-connected within the administration and known for his direct access to Trump, Gor has increasingly taken part in high-level diplomatic engagements, acquiring influence beyond his role as ambassador to India. He is also seen as an important link between Washington and several Asian countries, as well as a close confidant of secretary of state Marco Rubio According to the report, Gor's name has come up for several senior positions, including replacing Rubio as secretary of state or Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Some officials have also discussed the possibility of him taking over as deputy secretary of state from Chris Landau.Neither Rubio nor Wiles has indicated any intention of leaving their positions. However, speculation in Republican and State Department circles suggests Rubio could eventually leave the Cabinet to prepare for a potential presidential bid in 2028 or 2032.Wiles' position, meanwhile, is also believed to be under scrutiny within Trump's inner circle.Landau was also reportedly believed to be considering leaving after the midterms if Republicans lost control of Congress, anticipating potentially difficult congressional investigations. However, he subsequently denied having any plans to quit, telling The Sun that he had never indicated an intention to leave the State Department.Gor, however, dismissed the speculation, saying he had no interest in another position and had not discussed taking up a different role with anyone.Calling the report “complete and total b*******”, Gor praised Rubio as the most qualified and accomplished secretary of state, describing him as irreplaceable and a close friend. “I have zero interest in any other role,” he said.The State Department also rejected the claims. Assistant secretary for global public affairs Dylan Johnson said Rubio and Gor shared a strong professional relationship and personal friendship, dismissing the speculation as rumours based on anonymous sources. A White House official similarly described the report as fake, saying Gor had no interest in another position and believed Wiles and Rubio were doing a phenomenal job.Despite the denials, Gor's growing diplomatic profile has drawn attention within the administration. A Trump adviser told The Sun that the president “loves the guy”, crediting Gor with bringing deals to Trump during his years outside office rather than seeking favours from him.Since taking charge of the US embassy in New Delhi in November 2025, Gor has helped facilitate several high-level visits to India, including those by Rubio, commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and then-Army secretary Dan Driscoll. His responsibilities have also extended beyond India, with his dual role as ambassador and special envoy for South and Central Asia allowing him to participate in meetings with senior foreign officials, including Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.Rubio has visited India twice this year, and the two have travelled together frequently since Gor's appointment. They also appeared together in Atlanta at a G20 summit last week.Gor was also central to Rubio's visit to Uzbekistan last month, part of the Trump administration's efforts to deepen ties with resource-rich Central Asian countries. Born in Uzbekistan when it was part of the Soviet Union, Gor has used his background and regional connections in his additional role as special envoy for South and Central Asia.His approach to diplomacy is seen by some officials as closely aligned with Trump's emphasis on dealmaking and promoting American business interests.Gor, who worked on Trump's 2024 election campaign, has previously been linked to the business interests of the president's family. His publishing company has published Trump's books, and he is particularly close to Donald Trump Jr. Before leaving for India, Gor was sworn in as ambassador during an Oval Office ceremony at which Trump described him as a “great guy” and said he was “very proud” of him.His tenure in New Delhi has also attracted attention for his hands-on management style. According to two people familiar with the embassy's operations, Gor has exercised an unusual degree of control over personnel decisions, including pushing out career State Department employees and locally hired staff.Rubio had earlier defended Gor's appointment, telling The New York Times that his “access to the president” made him “an enormous asset” for both India and the State Department.However, whether Gor's connections would translate into a Senate-confirmed Cabinet position remains uncertain. All Senate Democrats voted against his confirmation as ambassador as part of a larger package of nominees.Before joining the Trump administration, Gor spent roughly a decade working on Capitol Hill, primarily for Republican senator Rand Paul. At the White House Office of Presidential Personnel, he was responsible for identifying and vetting candidates for thousands of political appointments across the federal government.
Article Summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has emerged as a possible contender for senior positions in president Donald Trump's administration. His name reportedly circulating for roles including White House chief of staff and secretary of state. Gor dismissed the speculation, saying he had no interest in another position and had not discussed taking up a different role.

Article Title: Maharashtra FDA suspends Mumbai's Cooper Hospital PPP blood bank licence; services halted till November 7
Article Text:
The FDA suspended the public-private-partnership blood bank license at Cooper Hospital due to documentation issues (File photo)





MUMBAI: The food and drug administration (FDA) has suspended public-private-partnership (PPP) blood bank licence at Cooper Hospital for two days starting today.The blood bank is run by Samarprit Bahuddeshiya Sevabhavi Vikas Sanstha and the services can only resume from midnight November 7.Hospital authorities said for the next two-three days they will be relying on blood bank at Trauma Hospital in Jogeshwari.Speaking to TOI, FDA officials said the notice was served to them 90-days prior. One of the contraventions found was lack of proper documentation.Last month, FDA had taken action against JJ Hospital and Nair Hospital blood banks and deans had to involve FDA minister Narhari Zirwal to secure a stay.The action was after the two hospitals were participants in the camp by a private group where watches had been gifted to donors at a blood donation drive organised in April on the occasion of a corporate bigwig’s birthday.
Article Summary: The blood bank is run by Samarprit Bahuddeshiya Sevabhavi Vikas Sanstha. The services can only resume from midnight November 7. Last month, FDA had taken action against JJ Hospital and Nair Hospital blood banks.
